title: Record kill-switch stops as killed; mark bound-only cost score provision
summary: Fixes minor m8 of the v0 acceptance review. When `athena stop` kills the producer's process group before the driver's once-a-second check, the invocation is now recorded as `killed` (reason: kill switch), not `error`. When an execution cost is only a bound, the `cost_usd` quantity score is marked provisional instead of resolving to a firm figure. The audience is the maintainer and the verifier, who read invocation records and scores.

defaults_applied.how: All changes are Rust code and tests.
New tests for the driver, the scorer, and the lifecycle; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Fixes both the driver's attribution race and the scorer's treatment of bound-only costs, not just the one stopped job.
Criteria check that the recorded outcome and provisional flag are produced in tests that exercise the behavior.
Behavior criteria name cargo commands the verifier can run.
One focused change on the two m8 symptoms.
Doc comments, docs and the CHANGELOG entry are written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Root cause 1: in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs the outcome is Killed only if the driver's own loop set `killed`. `athena stop` can kill the group first, so the child exits with no result and the invocation is recorded as Error. The fix checks `registry.stopped()` after the stream ends and, if it is on and there is no result, records Killed with a kill-switch detail.

Root cause 2: in crates/athena-score/src/lib.rs, `score_records` sums `best_lower()` of the execution invocations and scores that as a firm `cost_usd`. A killed or bound-only cost is only a lower bound, and the cap is the upper bound.

'Provisional' follows the existing `provisional` convention on event scores. I add a defaulted `provisional` field to the quantity score record (`QuantityScore` in athena-data), so existing records still parse. Provisional quantities are excluded from aggregates and skill, or at least flagged. The reader should check how the aggregates consume `quantities`.

A cost counts as 'only a bound' when any non-reader invocation's cost is not an exact measurement (killed, or the cost is a lower bound or estimate). The producer should use the existing Quantity type in athena-data/src/quantity.rs to tell exact from bounded.
Changing the score record shape may require bumping or extending the `RULES` string, because the commit gate recomputes scores and compares. If so, the gate and history tests are updated together.
Docs are touched only where the behavior is described (docs/records.md, docs/enforcement.md row M14, CHANGELOG).

acceptance_criteria.text: A new driver test in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs shows that a child ending with no result while the kill switch is on yields `InvocationOutcome::Killed` with a detail naming the kill switch, not `Error`. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.

A new scoring test in crates/athena-score builds a job whose execution cost is only a bound (a killed producer) and shows that the `cost_usd` quantity score is marked provisional. It also shows that a job with exact costs is not provisional. Run: cargo test -p athena-score.

An end-to-end test in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs shows that a producer stopped by the kill switch closes with a `killed` invocation record and a provisional cost score. The commit gate still accepts the recomputed score. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli.
The whole workspace passes `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` with no warnings, and `cargo fmt --check` is clean.
A bound-only cost is no longer scored as a firm figure. A provisional `cost_usd` score does not count in aggregates as a resolved value. This can be read in the score code and its test.
Older score.json records without the new field still deserialize, so existing job history in the repository is unaffected. A test or the unchanged history tests show this.
docs/records.md describes the provisional quantity field and the kill-switch attribution, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry citing m8 of docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-acceptance-1.md.

out_of_scope: The other minor findings of the v0 acceptance review (m1–m7, m9 and later)
Changing the kill switch's own mechanism, or adding a dedicated reason to the job's failure message beyond what recording the invocation as killed needs
Changing governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows, rust-toolchain.toml)
Re-scoring or rewriting existing job records in history
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass rate than the reference. The change spans the driver, the score record schema, and the commit gate's recomputation, which have to stay consistent.
